open_obligations.what_is_open: For every constant-rank relative-interior stratum of the observed-law image of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), construct a chart \(p(\zeta)\) whose differential exhausts that stratum's restricted tangent space, account for observationally equivalent latent representations, and evaluate for every reported direction \(a\) whether \((I-\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(S_P)})a^\top G_p\) is nonzero.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core supplies only prospective symbols \(\zeta\) and \(S_P\), not coordinates for cohort masses, type masses, initial laws, date-specific transition rows, their common-kernel equalities, or their support constraints. More importantly, \(\text{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\) deliberately leaves the type allocation of date-\(1\) absorbers unidentified. Thus the natural latent-primitive map is noninjective, may have representation-dependent Jacobians, and can meet itself or change rank at boundary strata. A derivative at one arbitrarily chosen latent representation is not proved to span the tangent space of the observed-law image. Until an atlas or an equivalent finite system of observable equality constraints is constructed and its rank is proved, \(\operatorname{col}(S_P)\) is undetermined. Projecting onto a postulated column space would assume the central step of the open question.
open_obligations.attempted: A natural candidate writes each legal observed cell as \(p_{d,x_0,\ldots,x_4}=\gamma_d\sum_{j=1}^J\pi_j^d\mu_j^d(x_0)H_j^d[x_0,x_1]Q_j[x_1,x_2]R_j^d[x_2,x_3]V_j^d[x_3,x_4]\), where all rows are stochastic on \(\mathcal G\), \(R_j^0=U_j\), \(R_j^1\) is the treated factual first-post kernel, and \(V_j^d\) is an unrestricted factual date-\(4\) kernel. Row-simplex coordinates make this a finite polynomial map, and differentiating it gives a candidate Jacobian. This route does not close because unreachable rows, label equivalences, and arbitrary type allocations among paths absorbed by date \(1\) yield nonunique primitive points above the same \(p\). The prior projection argument was also checked: it starts only after assuming that this candidate Jacobian spans the entire restricted score space, so it cannot establish the missing equality itself.
